title: Siraj Captains Hyderabad to Innings Win Over Tripura in Ranji Trophy
excerpt: Tanay Thyagarajan took nine wickets in the match and Aniketh Reddy five in the first innings as Hyderabad won by an innings and 40 runs; UP and Mumbai also won big.
body:
• Hyderabad beat Tripura by an innings and 40 runs in their Ranji Trophy Group B opener at the Gymkhana Ground, with Mohammed Siraj captaining the side.
  • Left-arm spinner Tanay Thyagarajan took 6 for 52 in the second innings for a nine-wicket match haul, after Aniketh Reddy's five-wicket haul in the first innings.
  • Tripura were bowled out for 134 and 120. Hyderabad's 294, built on Ruthik Yadav's 61 and Tanmay Agarwal's 54, was enough for an innings win and a bonus point.
  • Uttar Pradesh and Mumbai also won by an innings inside three days — UP by an innings and 267 runs over Bihar, Mumbai by an innings and 155 runs over Chandigarh.

Mohammed Siraj began his stint as Hyderabad captain with an innings victory, as his side beat Tripura by an innings and 40 runs in the opening round of the Ranji Trophy at the Gymkhana Ground. Hyderabad finished the match inside three days and took a bonus point from the Group B fixture.

Siraj, named captain for the first two matches, took two wickets in the second innings. The decisive bowling, though, came from Hyderabad's left-arm spinners on a pitch that favoured spin. That is the central fact of this match: Hyderabad's captain is one of India's leading fast bowlers, but his first win in charge was delivered by spin.

Spinners run through Tripura

Tripura chose to bat and were bowled out for 134 in the first innings. Aniketh Reddy took a five-wicket haul, finishing with 5 for 21 according to reports of the match, while Thyagarajan took three wickets. Bikramkumar Das made 50 and Hrituraj Roy 33, but the rest of the innings fell away against spin.

The second innings followed the same pattern, only faster. Tripura were bowled out for 120 in 41.2 overs, with Thyagarajan taking 6 for 52 to complete nine wickets in the match. Siraj took 2 for 19, while Ruthik Yadav and Abhirath Reddy took a wicket each. Sentu Sarkar top-scored with 27 in the second innings.

Aniketh credited mentor Wasim Jaffer's advice for part of the performance. He said Jaffer had urged the team to be stubborn — using the word "khadoos" — and to show character and grit in high-pressure situations, whether batting or bowling. Aniketh, 25, had bowled long spells in Hyderabad's senior Super League before the season and took six wickets in a practice match against Kerala, according to The New Indian Express report.

Lower order builds the lead

Hyderabad's batting was not straightforward. They replied with 294, a lead of 160, but needed the lower middle order to do it. Opener Tanmay Agarwal made 54 and Abhirath Reddy 32, before Gahlaut Rahul Singh, Pragnay Reddy and Kodimela Himateja fell cheaply.

No. 6 Ruthik Yadav made 61 off 150 balls on debut, Rahul Radesh made 40 off 119 balls and Chama Milind made 40 off 55. Sandip Sarkar took eight wickets for Tripura, a fine return in a losing cause, but 294 proved more than enough once Hyderabad's spinners went to work again. Hyderabad took seven points from the match as they look to reach the knockouts for the first time in a decade, according to the report.

UP and Mumbai win big

Uttar Pradesh produced the round's largest margin. Led by Aryan Juyal, UP made 540 against Bihar at the Rajgir International Cricket Stadium and won by an innings and 267 runs. Madhav Kaushik made 150 and Rinku Singh 112, with Aaradhya Yadav scoring 84 and Zeeshan Ansari 58. Bihar were bowled out for 141 and, following on, 132. Zeeshan Ansari took 4 for 40 in the second innings and Karan Sharma took seven wickets in the match.

Mumbai also won inside three days, beating Chandigarh by an innings and 155 runs at the Wankhede Stadium in Group D. Mumbai made 429, with captain Siddhesh Lad scoring 86, Musheer Khan 65, Tanush Kotian 58 and Mohit Awasthi an unbeaten 56. Chandigarh were bowled out for 78 in the first innings and 196 in the second, with Shams Mulani taking 3 for 69 and Kotian 3 for 30 in the second innings. Mumbai, like Hyderabad and UP, took a bonus point.

What's next

For Hyderabad, the test now is whether this spin-led formula travels. The opening win gives Siraj's side early momentum in Group B, and it gives their two left-arm spinners confidence before tougher fixtures. For the diaspora reader, the round was also a reminder that the Ranji Trophy's opening week still produces the domestic game's clearest storylines — an India fast bowler learning captaincy at home, and spinners deciding the match he led.
